# 3. Data sources, distilled (for TypeScript reimplementation)

From `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py` (1325 lines; deployed as `~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py`).

| Agent | Tag | Storage | How enumerated |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | `[oc]` | `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` | `SELECT id, directory, title, time_updated FROM session WHERE time_archived IS NULL ORDER BY time_updated DESC` (opened `file:<db>?mode=ro`) |
| Claude Code | `[cc]` | `~/.claude/projects/**/<sessionId>.jsonl` | `rglob("*.jsonl")`, skip any path containing `/subagents/`, `sid = filename stem`, sort by `st_mtime` DESC |
| Codex | `[cx]` | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` | `rglob("rollout-*.jsonl")`; sid from `session_meta.payload.id`, fallback UUID regex on filename. Titles also read from `~/.codex/session_index.jsonl` (`{id, thread_name}`) |
| Cursor Agent CLI | `[cu]` | `~/.cursor/chats/<wsHash>/<chatId>/store.db` | glob `*/*/store.db`; content is opaque BLOBs |
| Cursor IDE | `[ci]` | `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/{globalStorage,workspaceStorage}` → `state.vscdb`, table `cursorDiskKV`, keys `composerData:<id>` and `bubbleId:<composerId>:<bubbleId>` | Linux fallback `~/.config/Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb` |

**Claude JSONL parsing** (`_claude_first_user_msg`): reads only the first **80 lines** (`MAX_LINES_SCAN`); `cwd` comes from the first record with a `cwd` key; title is the first record with `type == "user"` whose `message.content` (string, or the first `{type:"text"}` part of a list) does not start with any of:
```
<local-command-caveat>, <local-command-stdout>, <local-command-stderr>,
<system-reminder>, <command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>,
<environment_context>, <user_instructions>, <INSTRUCTIONS>,
# AGENTS.md, # AGENTS instructions, Caveat:
```
Snippets are truncated to 140 chars with `…`.

**SpecStory reverse-lookup**: scans `*.md` in `$SPECSTORY_HISTORY_DIRS` (colon-separated; default `~/.local/share/chezmoi/.specstory/history`), first 10 lines each, regex `Session ([0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12})`, builds `{sid → path}`.

**tmux pane enumeration** — the exact format string:
```
tmux list-panes -aF '#{session_name}\t#{window_index}\t#{window_name}\t#{pane_index}\t#{pane_id}\t#{pane_pid}\t#{pane_current_command}\t#{pane_current_path}\t#{pane_active}'
```
Target is assembled as `f"{session_name}:{window_index}.{pane_index}"`.

**Agent → pane resolution**:
- Claude is authoritative: for each `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, parse `{sessionId, cwd, status, name, updatedAt|startedAt}`, then walk the parent chain from that PID via `ps -o ppid= -p <pid>` (max 20 hops) until the PID matches a tmux `pane_pid`.
- Others: `pgrep -x codex|opencode|cursor-agent` for binaries; for Node-wrapped CLIs, `ps -axo pid=,comm=,args=` and match `comm ∈ {node,bun,deno}` with `"/" + needle` in argv.
- Process start time floor: `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>`, parsed with `"%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y"` / `"%a %b  %d %H:%M:%S %Y"` — prevents a fresh session inheriting an older session's title from the same cwd.
- Codex cwd lookup is bounded to the **last 7 days**.
- Sort order: agent priority `{[cc]:0, [cx]:1, [oc]:2, [cu]:3}`, then `-when_ts`. Status glyphs `{busy:"●", idle:"○"}` are pre-rendered in Python because TV's display template can't do per-column substitution.

From `executable_agent-wakeup.py` (681 lines):
- pane capture: `tmux capture-pane -p -S -120 -t <target>`; pane id resolution `tmux display-message -p -t <target> '#{pane_id}'`
- pueue read: `pueue status --json`, filter `task.label` startswith `agent-wakeup:` and status != `Done`; pane_id = label suffix
- group bootstrap: `pueue group add agent-wakeup` then `pueue parallel -g agent-wakeup 1`
- schedule: `pueue add -g agent-wakeup --label "agent-wakeup:<paneid>" --delay <delay> --print-task-id "<script> send-now --pane <pane> …"`
- cancel: `pueue remove <id>` (falls back to `pueue kill <id>` then remove)
- send: `tmux send-keys -t <pane> C-u "continue" Enter`, or `tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter` for rate-limit menus
- quota regexes: `\b(?:session limit|rate limit|limit reached|quota)\b|\bhit your\b.+?\blimit\b`; reset `\bresets?\b(?:\s+in)?\s+([^)\n\r]+)`; menu `(/rate-limit-options|stop and wait for limit to reset|what do you want to do\?)`
- states emitted: `SCHEDULED`, `WAIT_MENU`, `READY`, `WAIT_QUOTA`, `ACTIVE`, `IDLE`, `UNKNOWN`, `ORPHAN`

# 5. Gotchas that will bite a reimplementation

- **Bare `{` breaks everything.** Any literal `{...}` in a TV preview/action command string (outside TV's own `{split:…}` / `{strip_ansi}` placeholders) silently disables **all** placeholder substitution in that same string. Documented at `pitfalls/tv-channel-bare-braces-break-substitution.md`, which is why all the rich logic lives in Python helpers.
- **`status` is read-only in zsh** — `agent-panes.toml` preview deliberately names the variable `pane_status`.
- **Glyph mapping must be pre-computed**, not done in the display template.
- `glow --style auto` degrades to plain when stdout is a pipe (always true in TV's preview), hence `--style dark` in `agent-panes.toml`.
- The pueue channel's `output` is column 0 (task id) — the `filter_group` action detects a non-numeric id to distinguish a group row from a task row.
- Backslash escaping differs between the `.toml` and `.toml.tmpl` files (templates need doubled backslashes for chezmoi's Go-template pass).

# Pueue-Raycast-Extension — architecture report

## 0. The governing philosophy (read this first)

Three ideas explain nearly every file:

1. **Every comment states a verified fact and its consequence, not a description of the code.** Comments read like `"Measured, not guessed. Killing a running task and polling status --json until Done, five trials: min 278 ms median 284 ms max 297 ms"`. Prose says *what was observed*, *what was tried and failed*, and *why the obvious thing is wrong*. This is the strongest replicable trait.
2. **Purity as a testing strategy.** There is no test runner. Instead, modules that hold logic (`normalize.ts`, `argv.ts`, `errors.ts`, `connections.ts`, `ssh.ts`, `logfile.ts`, `optimistic.ts`) are kept **free of `@raycast/api` imports** so a single `dev-check.ts` can be compiled with the already-installed `tsc` and run under plain `node`. Import discipline *is* the test harness.
3. **Knowledge is externalized into three separate stores** — `TODO.md` (index of future work), `backlog/` (design notes for undecided items), `pitfalls/` (symptom-titled, grep-able trap docs) — plus a vendored agent skill that generalizes the lessons for the *next* extension.

## 3. `src/` structure and key abstractions

### The layering rule

```
views (tsx)  →  lib/pueue/index.ts (barrel)  →  transport interface  →  cli-transport
                     ↑
   pure helpers (normalize, optimistic, format) imported directly by dev-check
```

`src/lib/pueue/index.ts` says it explicitly: *"The public API. Views import from here and nowhere else inside `pueue/`."* It re-exports types, normalizers, connections, error predicates, binary resolvers, then exposes flat function wrappers: `status()`, `groups()`, `logs()`, `mutate()`, `follow()`, `probe()`, `snapshot()`, `readLogText()`, `taskEnvs()`.

The **one deliberate violation** is `optimistic.ts`, which imports from `./pueue/normalize` and `./pueue/types` directly rather than the barrel — with a comment explaining why: *"the barrel pulls in the transport and therefore @raycast/api, and this module must stay runnable outside Raycast so `just verify` can assert it."*

### The transport seam (`transport.ts`)

Types-only, no runtime imports, so `cli-transport.ts` can depend on it without a cycle. The factory lives in `index.ts` for the same reason.

```ts
export interface PueueTransport {
  readState(o?: StatusOptions): Promise<State>;
  readGroups(o?: ConnectionOption & {signal?: AbortSignal}): Promise<GroupMap>;
  readLogs(ids: number[], o?: LogOptions): Promise<LogMap>;
  mutate(m: Mutation, o?: ConnectionOption): Promise<number | void>;
  followLog(id, lines, h: FollowHandlers, o?): () => void;   // returns cancel
  probe(o?): Promise<{version: string; major: number; reachable: boolean}>;
}
```

**The single most reusable idea in the repo** — mutations are a **data union**, never argv:

```ts
export type Mutation =
  | { op: "add"; command: string; group?: string; label?: string; priority?: number;
      workingDirectory?: string; after?: number[]; delay?: string;
      stashed?: boolean; immediate?: boolean; escape?: boolean }
  | { op: "kill"; ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean; signal?: string }
  | { op: "restart"; ids: number[]; inPlace?: boolean; ... }
  | ... 16 variants total
```

With the rationale stated in the module docstring: *"The seam only holds because mutations are modelled as data. If `mutate` took a `string[]` of argv, a socket transport would have to parse argv back into intent — which is not a seam, it is a shell."*

`setTransport(t)` exists as the testing / future-transport hook; `transport()` lazily memoizes `createCliTransport()`.

### Types (`types.ts`) — literal transcription, not ergonomics

Deliberately a 1:1 copy of pueue_lib v4.0.4's serde output, with the ergonomic view built on top in `normalize.ts`. Key facts encoded as types:

- `TaskStatus` is **externally tagged and recursive** through `Locked`: `{Running: {enqueued_at, start}}`, `{Locked: {previous_status: TaskStatus}}`, etc. There is no flat `"status": "Running"` anywhere in v4.
- `TaskResult` mixes bare strings and single-field objects: `"Success"` but `{"Failed": 127}`.
- The one-letter split: `Stashed` carries `enqueue_at` (future), everything else carries `enqueued_at` (past).
- `RawTask` has `envs`; the app-facing `Task = Omit<RawTask, "envs">`.
- `GroupMap` (from `group --json`) is a *different top level* from `State` (from `status --json`) — the type comment calls confusing them "the easiest bug in this codebase", and `readState` has a runtime guard for it.

### Normalizers (`normalize.ts`) — pure, React-free

`statusKind`, `unwrapLocked` (recursive), `underlyingKind`, `taskResult`, `resultKind`, `exitCode`, `spawnError`, predicates (`isDone/isRunning/isFailed/isActive/hasEverRun`), timestamp accessors (`enqueuedAt/startedAt/endedAt/durationMs`) with a guarded `parseTs` (because `new Date(null)` returns 1970 rather than Invalid Date), `statusLabel`, `statusKeywords`, `oneline`, `taskList`, plus log helpers `isPueueErrorOutput` / `cleanLogOutput`.

`isFailed` is an **allowlist** on purpose: "a denylist would miss whichever variant pueue adds next". `StatusKind` includes an `"unknown"` member so a newer pueue degrades rather than throws.

### Errors (`errors.ts`)

```ts
type PueueErrorKind = "binary-not-found" | "config-missing" | "daemon-not-running"
                    | "host-unreachable" | "bad-query" | "bad-arguments"
                    | "timeout" | "command-failed";

class PueueError extends Error {
  readonly kind: PueueErrorKind;
  readonly detail: string;      // ANSI-stripped, eyre-noise-stripped, ready to render
  readonly exitCode: number | null;
  readonly argv: readonly string[];
}
```

Pipeline: `cleanStderr()` (strips SGR escapes — color_eyre emits them even to a pipe; truncates at `Location:`; strips eyre's `0:`/`1:` cause numbering; filters a `NOISE_PATTERNS` list containing the protocol-version warning that would otherwise become the toast title) → `firstLine()` → `classify(detail, exitCode)` (ordered most-specific-first, matching strings *captured* from 4.0.4) → `fromExecError(e, argv)` (handles ENOENT and execFile's SIGTERM-means-timeout quirk). Exported predicates `isBinaryMissing/isDaemonDown/isBadQuery/isHostUnreachable` are what the UI branches on.

`fixtures/stderr.json` holds all 7 failure shapes byte-exact; `dev-check.ts` asserts every one buckets correctly.

---

## 4. How it shells out to `pueue`

### Binary resolution — the launchd PATH trap (`binary.ts`)

The module docstring names it *"the #1 hazard in a Raycast extension"*. Raycast runs extensions in a managed Node process under launchd, which never sources a shell rc, so `PATH ≈ /usr/bin:/bin` and a bare `pueue` fails with `spawn pueue ENOENT`. **A terminal hides this completely** — `ray develop`'s console inherits your full PATH — so anything touched there must be tested from Raycast root search.

```ts
const PROBE_DIRS = [
  "/opt/homebrew/bin",              // Apple Silicon Homebrew
  "/usr/local/bin",                 // x86_64 Homebrew, incl. under Rosetta
  join(homedir(), ".cargo", "bin"),
  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
  "/usr/bin", "/bin",
];
```

`resolvePueue()`: preference first (**consulted before the module cache** so a change takes effect immediately) and `existsSync`-validated (so a stale path degrades into the probe rather than an unexplained ENOENT), then the cache, then the probe; throws `PueueError("binary-not-found")`. `resolvePueued()` prefers the **sibling** of the resolved client, because a Homebrew client + cargo daemon is version skew and pueue v4 broke the wire protocol.

Also here: `baseEnv()` (passes HOME through; NO_COLOR deliberately *not* set, with a note that it was verified to have no effect), `pueueDirectory()` (regex-probes pueue.yml for `pueue_directory:` rather than adding a YAML dep), `taskLogPath(id)`, `resolveBrew()`, and `isBrewManagedDaemon()` — which gates the one-click "Start Daemon" action because *starting `pueued -d` from Raycast makes the daemon a child of Raycast's launchd process, so every task it ever runs inherits Raycast's minimal environment.* That is "the same PATH problem, except it silently poisons every future task instead of failing loudly once."

### The subprocess layer (`cli-transport.ts`)

Docstring lists the three CLI facts that shape everything: only `status`/`log`/`group` emit JSON; global flags must precede the subcommand; `status --json` embeds a per-task env snapshot.

- **Single funnel**: every call goes through `run(args, opts)` so failures classify uniformly. `execFile` promisified — **never `shell: true`**.
- **Global args**: `["--color", "never", ...(cfg ? ["--config", cfg] : [])]` placed *before* the subcommand. `--config` is how a connection is selected, which is why remote support needs zero protocol code.
- **Buffers/timeouts**: `BIG_BUFFER = 64 MB` (the 1 MB default would truncate a large status/log into a JSON parse error); `READ_TIMEOUT_MS 10_000`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS 15_000`, `SSH_TIMEOUT_MS 15_000` (reduced from 30 s after an unreachable host blocked the menu bar).
- **JSON parsing**: `parseJson<T>(stdout, what)` wraps `JSON.parse` into a `PueueError("command-failed", "Could not parse ${what} as JSON")`. `readState` additionally validates `"tasks" in raw` to guard against ever being handed `group --json`'s shape (which would silently yield zero tasks). `readGroups` unwraps `{groups}` if present, in case upstream ever aligns the shapes. `readLogs` treats `{}` for an unknown id as an empty result, not an error.
- **Secret stripping at the parse boundary**: `stripEnvs()` deletes `envs` from every task *before it can reach `useCachedPromise`'s disk-backed Cache*, which would otherwise write every secret in the submitting shell's environment to disk in plaintext. `taskEnvs(id)` re-reads on demand, uncached, never from a render path.
- **`mutate`** returns `void` except for `add`, coaxed into printing an id with `--print-task-id`.
- **`followLog`** uses `spawn`, accumulates stderr, and treats a zero exit code as *completion, not failure* (`pueue follow` exits when the task stops). Returns a cancel closure that SIGTERMs the child.
- **`probe`** parses the version *shape* (`/^pueue\s+(\d+)\.(\d+)/`) rather than inferring capability from an exit code, and assumes v4 when unparseable.

Two functions live **outside** the transport by design: `readTaskEnvs` (bypasses the transport because the transport's whole job for that field is to throw it away) and `readLogFromDisk` (guarded by `readsLocalLogs(connection)` — *"a remote daemon's logs are not on this disk, but the local log directory usually exists, so an unguarded read returns a different task's output under the same id"*).

### argv (`argv.ts`) — pure, and cross-checked against `--help`

`argvFor(m: Mutation): string[]` plus `subcommandOf()` and `longFlagsOf()` helpers that exist *specifically so `dev-check.ts` can shell out to the real `pueue <sub> --help` and assert every emitted flag actually exists*. That's the standout testing trick: 16 representative mutations with every optional field set, each cross-checked live against the binary's own help text.

The `add` builder ends with `a.push("--", m.command)` as **one argv element** — "pueue joins its variadic `<COMMAND>...` with spaces and hands the result to `sh -c`, so quoting it here would double-escape it. Never build a shell string." `restart` always emits an explicit `--in-place`/`--not-in-place` because the default comes from the user's config.

### Remote (`connections.ts` + `ssh.ts`)

Connection modes: `local | ssh | socket`. The preference is a single-line textfield (Raycast has no multi-line preference type) parsed on `[\n;]` with `|` field separators; unparseable lines are returned as `invalid` and **rendered in the UI**, because "silently ignoring a line someone typed is indistinguishable from a bug". A bare host is a complete config.

`ssh.ts` covers quoting (`shellQuote` with the `'\''` trick, `quoteRemotePath` using *double* quotes so `~`/`$HOME` survive to the far side) and multiplexing (`ControlMaster=auto`, `ControlPath=/tmp/pueue-rc-%C` — `%C` is a short hash, and `/tmp` because Raycast support paths blow the ~104-byte unix socket limit — `ControlPersist=120`). Measured: 200–400 ms unmultiplexed vs **10–30 ms** multiplexed vs 22–44 ms for a *local* pueue. Plus `reachabilityArgs()` (`ConnectTimeout=5`, `ServerAliveInterval=5`, `ServerAliveCountMax=3`) and `BatchMode=yes`, with `isSshUnreachable()`/`isRemoteBinaryMissing()` classifiers so an ssh problem isn't filed under "Pueue command failed".

---

## 5. State management patterns

### `useCachedPromise` conventions

**Every fetcher dependency is an argument, never a closure capture** — with the comment explaining that the argument array is the cache key:

```ts
const state = useCachedPromise(
  (g: string, q: string, connectionName: string) =>
    readStatus({ group: g === ALL_GROUPS ? undefined : g, query: q,
                 signal: stateAbort.current?.signal,
                 connection: connectionByName(connectionName) }),
  [group, query, conn.connection.name],
  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: stateAbort },
);
```

**One `AbortController` ref per independent read** — `stateAbort` and `groupsAbort` are separate "so a superseded state read must not cancel an in-flight group read".

**`execute:` for conditional fetches** — the detail-pane log preview runs only when the pane is open *and* `hasEverRun(selectedTask)`, with `keepPreviousData: false` because it's per-selection.

**`onData` side effect** — the menu bar uses `onData` to call `updateCommandMetadata({subtitle})`.

### Optimistic updates + delayed reconcile (`optimistic.ts` + `actions.tsx`)

This is the second most reusable pattern. The daemon acks *before* its update loop applies the change (measured: ack ~22 ms, applied ~280 ms later; five trials min 278 / median 284 / max 297 ms). `useCachedPromise`'s `mutate` revalidates immediately by default, which reads pre-change state and visibly undoes the action.

```ts
await state.mutate(runMutation(mutation, {connection}), {
  optimisticUpdate: (data) => optimistic(data, mutation),
  rollbackOnError: true,
  shouldRevalidateAfter: false,     // "The load-bearing line."
});
setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_DELAY_MS);   // 400
setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_SETTLE_MS);  // 1500
nudgeMenuBar();
```

Two reads, not one pessimistic one: "rather than pick a pessimistic single delay that makes every action feel sluggish, read twice."

`act<T>()` is **generic over the cached shape** because Tasks caches `State` and Groups caches `GroupMap`; each supplies its own pure updater. Two bound wrappers: `actOnTasks` / `actOnGroups`. `ActOptions` carries `verb` (present continuous → animated toast title), `done` (past tense → success), optional `confirm` (gated on the `confirmDestructive` preference, with `rememberUserChoice`), and `connection`. Returns `boolean` (false = cancelled at the confirm).

`applyMutation(state, m)` is **pure and total**: never throws, never mutates in place (asserted), and — crucially — **returns its input unchanged when the outcome is unknowable**: `add` (new id), `switch` (reordering), `send`, and a non-in-place `restart` all return `state`. Even starting a *queued* task is not predicted, because "a queued task only starts if a slot is free; predicting that needs the scheduler". `targets()` resolves `ids | group | all` against actual task states. Group-side effects are modelled (killing a group also pauses it; removing a group moves tasks to `default`) because they're real pueue behavior.

### Cross-command coordination

`nudgeMenuBar()` fires `launchCommand({name: "queue-menu", type: LaunchType.Background})` after `RECONCILE_DELAY_MS`, `.catch(() => {})` because it throws when the target command is disabled (the normal state for store installs). Called from `actions.tsx`, `add-task.tsx`, and `quick-add.tsx`.

The menu bar → Tasks jump uses `launchCommand(..., {context: {logTaskId, connectionName}})`, and the receiving side guards with `pushedLog = useRef(false)` **and** waits for the connection to actually become active before pushing — "task ids are per-daemon; pushing early opens whichever daemon was selected before, which looks like it worked and shows someone else's task with the same id. Observed, not theorised."

### Persistence key scoping

`useCachedState` and `LocalStorage` keys are **scoped by connection**: `tasks.group:${conn.name}`, `add.group:${conn.name}`, `add.cwd:${conn.name}`. The comment: "a single shared key meant switching to another machine left the list filtered by a group that only exists elsewhere, showing nothing. Observed. Scoping the key makes the mistake unrepresentable instead of merely corrected." The connection selection itself shares one key (`connection.name`) across views *and* the menu bar so they never disagree.

### The `structural` staleness flag (`error-states.tsx`)

`ErrorDescriptor` is one data shape with three renderers (`ErrorEmptyView`, `StaleBannerItem`, `ErrorDetail`), plus the menu bar consuming `describeError()` directly. Actions are **data** (`{id, title, icon, copy? | url? | run?}`) so each surface maps them to its own primitive.

`structural: boolean` drives the rendering decision:

| situation | render |
|---|---|
| first read failed, no data | `<List><ErrorEmptyView/></List>` — whole screen |
| structural failure + cached data | `StaleBannerItem` row atop the list |
| transient failure | ordinary toast |

Rationale: "`useCachedPromise` keeps serving its last successful read when a fetch fails, which is the right default — but with the daemon stopped it means a dead queue renders as a live one, and Raycast's failure toast is a single line at the bottom that scrolls away."

---

## 6. The menu bar command (`src/queue-menu.tsx`, 653 lines)

Four constraints are enumerated at the top of the file:

1. **No badge API** — the count *is* the `title`, `undefined` removes it. `menuTitle()` returns `undefined` when the chosen counts are all zero.
2. **`isLoading` is a contract, not a hint** — unset → Raycast renders then immediately unloads; stuck true → the whole tree re-runs every tick.
3. **Raycast restores the item from a database on restart**, not by re-running the command, so a stale render outlives a restart. Hence `snapshot()` returning `{state, fetchedAt}` as *one cache entry* ("so the two can never drift") and a disabled `Updated HH:MM` row.
4. **No `confirmAlert`** — it presents in the Raycast window, which is closed while the menu is open. Destructive items go behind `⌥` via `alternate`, and that gating honours the *same* `confirmDestructive` preference (the most recent commit, "Let the confirmations preference actually turn off ⌥").

Other implemented rules: every item title is prefixed with the task id ("identical siblings get their onAction handlers crossed"); `maxItemsPerSection` collapses overflow into an `…and N more` item that launches Tasks ("a 400-task queue must not become 400 menu items every minute"); feedback is `showHUD`, not `showToast`; **never return `null` on error** — an `ErrorMenu` renders instead; and the connection switcher is rendered in **both** the normal menu and the error menu, because "selecting a remote that turns out to be unreachable renders the error menu, and if the switcher only lived in the normal menu there would be no way back to Local. Escape routes have to live in the broken state, not only in the working one."

Icon is `assets/pueue-menubar.svg`, a monochrome template tinted at runtime — Red if any failure, Orange if all groups paused, PrimaryText otherwise: "the shape never moves in the menu bar, only its colour."

---

## 7. Testing setup

**No vitest, no jest, no test runner at all** — deliberate: "There is no test runner in a Raycast extension and adding one is store review noise."

Instead `src/lib/dev-check.ts` (1,064 lines) is a plain script run by:

```
just verify   # npx tsc --outDir .build/verify ... src/lib/dev-check.ts && node .build/verify/dev-check.js
```

A 10-line `check(name, actual, expected)` compares `JSON.stringify` and increments a `failures` counter; the script sets `process.exitCode` at the end. What it covers, section by section:

- status enum tagging, `Locked` unwrapping (incl. nested), result kinds, exit codes, spawn errors
- failure classification, timestamps (`enqueue_at` vs `enqueued_at`), durations, labels, keywords
- **stderr fixtures** — for all 7 captured shapes: no ANSI survives, no `Location:` block, correct `PueueErrorKind`, `message` is the first line
- **argv shape** + a **live cross-check**: `execFileSync(PUEUE_BIN, [...subcommand, "--help"])` and assert every long flag appears in the real help output, for all 16 mutation variants (skipped gracefully if the binary is absent)
- log-output handling (pueue's `(Pueue error)` in the `output` field, exit 0)
- optimistic updates over both `State` and `GroupMap`, including "the input state is never mutated in place" and "add is never predicted"
- connection parsing (valid + invalid lines), remote-path quoting, transport selection, `readsLocalLogs`, ssh reachability args, unreachable-host detection, shell quoting
- `readLogTail` against a real temp file (truncation, line-boundary trim, missing file)

Mocking is done by **fixtures, not mocks**: `fixtures/state.json` (12 tasks covering stashed/scheduled/queued/running/paused/locked/done×6-result-variants, with a `SECRET_TOKEN` in `envs` to prove stripping) and `fixtures/stderr.json` (7 byte-exact stderr captures). The only "mock" is the ad-hoc `{killed, signal, stderr}` objects fed to `fromExecError`.

`PUEUE_BIN` is re-probed locally in `dev-check.ts` because `binary.ts` imports `@raycast/api`, which only exists inside Raycast.

---

## 8. Docs, TODO, backlog, pitfalls

**No CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md exists.** Project knowledge lives in the three-store harness instead.

### `TODO.md` — the single index

Tagged `[S]`/`[M]`/`[L]` for effort, `P?` for "shape not decided, note in `backlog/`". Sections: **Next**, **Docs site**, **v0.3.0 candidates**, **Later**, **Deferred with notes**, **Won't do**. The "Won't do" section is unusual and valuable — it records *why* something was rejected with the verification (`--escape` collapses the command line; `pueue parallel` with no arg is broken in 4.0.4).

### `backlog/` — 5 design notes

Each answers *what, why it isn't done, what would have to be true to do it*, with a `**Status:** P? · **Effort:** [L]` header: `socket-transport.md` (CBOR unix socket — the transport seam exists for exactly this), `ai-tools.md`, `callback-notifications.md`, `store-publishing.md` (a checked checklist; only screenshots outstanding), `launchd-jobs-extension.md` (explicitly out of scope, "recorded because the question was asked").

### `pitfalls/` — 9 docs, titled by **symptom**

"One file per trap, titled by the symptom you'd search for — not the root cause, which you don't know yet when you're looking." Each opens with a **`## Symptoms (grep this section)`** block containing verbatim error text, then `## Cause`, then `## Fix`. The README is a symptom→file table. Files: launchd PATH, `--color` before subcommand, externally-tagged status enum, `pueue log` hiding errors in `output`, daemon state lag after a mutation, `ray build` not typechecking, cached list rendering a dead queue, remote working-directory FailedToSpawn, Raycast preferences can't be multiline.

### `docs/` — bilingual MkDocs site

6 pages × 2 languages using `mkdocs-static-i18n` **suffix** structure (`remote.md` / `remote.zh-TW.md`) with `fallback_to_default: true`. Pages: `index`, `getting-started` (287 lines), `remote` (200), `pueue-json-contract` (199 — "the assertions in `src/lib/dev-check.ts` are the executable version of this file"), `raycast-surfaces` (116 — the complete list of Raycast entry points and why there's no widget API), `prior-art` (55 — Brew/Colima/OrbStack/Yabai as precedent for requiring a pre-installed binary). Plugins: i18n, search, `llmstxt` (emits `/llms.txt` + `llms-full.txt`), `copy-to-llm`. Deployed by `.github/workflows/docs.yml` via uv + GitHub Pages.

`README.md` leads with a "Background refresh is off by default" section — "This is the single most likely 'it's broken' report, and it isn't a bug in the extension."

---

## 9. The vendored `raycast-extension-dev` skill

Lives at **`.agents/skills/raycast-extension-dev/`** (source of truth), symlinked from `.claude/skills/raycast-extension-dev`. Tracked in `skills-lock.json` with source `daviddwlee84/agent-skills`, `skillPath: skills/local/raycast-extension-dev/SKILL.md`, and a content hash. Four other skills are vendored the same way: `project-knowledge-harness`, `agent-history-hygiene`, `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`, `pueue-job-queue`.

Structure:

```
SKILL.md                                 the hub (~300 lines)
references/  runtime-and-subprocess.md (272)  manifest-and-commands.md (273)
             ui-patterns.md (256)  data-and-state.md (227)
             menu-bar.md (215)  store-publishing.md (193)
assets/      Justfile.template  tsconfig.json.template  eslint.config.mjs.template
             package.json.template  dev-check.ts.template  transport.ts.template
             error-descriptor.tsx.template  metadata-README.md.template
             extension-icon.placeholder.png (512×512, sha-pinned)
scripts/     new-raycast-extension.sh (386)   check-store-readiness.sh (324)
```

It is explicitly the **generalized extract of this repo**: "Every claim here was paid for once in a shipped extension; the `## Gotchas` section is the compressed bill." Contents: **the gate** (a table of what `tsc`/`dev-check`/`ray lint`/`ray build`/`ray build -e dist` each catch and miss), **the surface map**, **repo layout** (the extension IS the repo root; `ray publish` copies the *directory*, not the git index), and six workflows — A scaffold/retrofit, B wrap-a-CLI-behind-a-transport-seam, C data/cache/mutations, D failure-states-as-data, E the menu bar, F ship to the store. Then ~30 one-paragraph gotchas.

`check-store-readiness.sh` exists because **`ray lint` exits 0 with a completely empty `metadata/`**; it emits a JSON array of `{id, status, detail, fix}` with statuses `pass|warn|fail|skip` (skip explicitly *not* a pass) and exit codes 0/1/2/3/4. It's wired in as `just preflight`, which refuses with instructions if the skill isn't vendored.

The skill's "Deliberately absent, so nobody re-adds them" section is worth copying wholesale as a design idea.

---

## 10. Lint / typecheck / build tooling

**`tsconfig.json`** — `strict`, `isolatedModules`, `jsx: "react-jsx"`, `module: "commonjs"`, `target: ES2022`, `lib: ES2023`, `resolveJsonModule` (for the fixtures). The load-bearing line is `"include": ["src/**/*", "raycast-env.d.ts"]` — omit the second entry and the generated `Preferences` globals are invisible to `tsc`.

**`eslint.config.mjs`** — six lines: `defineConfig([...raycastConfig])` from `@raycast/eslint-config`. Prettier runs through `ray lint`.

**`Justfile`** — where the real workflow lives. Every recipe self-bootstraps with `([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) &&` because `ray` ships inside `@raycast/api`. Recipes:

| recipe | what |
|---|---|
| `dev` / `build` / `lint` / `fix` | thin `npm run` wrappers |
| `typecheck` | `npx tsc --noEmit` — "`ray build` bundles but does NOT typecheck — it happily shipped a State/GroupMap mismatch and a ReactNode clash" |
| `verify` | compile + run `dev-check.ts` |
| **`check`** | `typecheck verify lint build` — the pre-commit gate |
| `ci` | `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && just check` — proves the lockfile |
| `dist` | `npx ray build -e dist` — the build the store produces, and the one that *does* typecheck |
| `preflight` | the vendored store-readiness script |
| `shots` | interactive screenshot session; seeds fixtures, walks commands by deeplink, leaves only the keypress |
| `store-export` | rsync **allowlist** into `.build/store`, then `npm ci && ray lint && ray build -e dist` — because `ray publish` copies the directory and `docs/`, `site/`, `.venv/`, `.specstory/` would ride into the review PR |
| `fixtures` | seeds a local queue covering several status variants |

**CI** (`.github/workflows/extension.yml`) runs on a **macOS runner** (the toolchain is macOS-shaped), Node **22** (Raycast's runtime — "building against a newer one would let an API through here that throws inside Raycast"), `npm ci` (doubles as the lockfile proof), then `just check` and `just dist`. It invokes `just` rather than inlining the four commands "so CI and the local gate cannot drift apart."

---

## What I'd carry into a sibling repo, ranked

1. **The `lib/<backend>/` package with a types-only `transport.ts` seam and a `Mutation` data union.** Everything else follows from it.
2. **The import-discipline-as-test-harness rule** + a single `dev-check.ts` + JSON fixtures + the live `--help` cross-check for generated argv.
3. **`act<T>()`**: optimistic update → `shouldRevalidateAfter: false` → two delayed revalidates at measured intervals → sibling-command nudge. Plus the "return input unchanged when unknowable" rule for the pure predictor.
4. **`ErrorDescriptor` as data with a `structural` flag** and N renderers; actions as `{copy? | url? | run?}` data.
5. **Absolute-binary resolution** with preference-before-cache, `existsSync` validation, and both Homebrew prefixes.
6. **Strip secret-bearing fields at the parse boundary**, not at render time, because `useCachedPromise` persists to disk.
7. **Scope every `useCachedState`/`LocalStorage` key** by whatever the value belongs to.
8. **The Justfile as the real workflow** (`check = typecheck verify lint build`), CI calling `just` so they can't drift, and an allowlist `store-export`.
9. **The three-store knowledge harness** — `TODO.md` (with a "Won't do" section), `backlog/` (what/why-not/what-would-have-to-be-true), `pitfalls/` (symptom-titled, with a grep-able verbatim-error block).
10. **The comment style**: state the measurement, the thing you tried that failed, and the consequence of getting it wrong. Every non-obvious line has one.

**Field → meaning map:**

| Need | Field | Present on |
|---|---|---|
| session id | `sessionId` | every record type |
| cwd | `cwd` | `user`, `assistant`, `attachment`, `system` |
| model | `message.model` (e.g. `claude-opus-5`) | `assistant` only |
| timestamp | `timestamp` (ISO 8601 UTC, ms) | `user`, `assistant`, `attachment`, `system` |
| role | `message.role` + top-level `type` | `user` / `assistant` |
| summary/title | `aiTitle` (`type:"ai-title"`), `agentName`, `slug` | metadata lines |
| tokens/cost | `message.usage.{input,output,cache_creation,cache_read}_tokens` | `assistant` |
| git branch | `gitBranch` | `user`/`assistant` |
| CLI version | `version` (`2.1.220`) | `user`/`assistant` |
| subagent | `isSidechain:true`, plus `subagents/agent-*.jsonl` | — |

`ai-title` / `last-prompt` are **appended repeatedly** (once per turn), so take the *last* occurrence.

Tiny sessions can be metadata-only — e.g. `/Users/david/.claude/projects/-Users-david-Documents-Program-Pueue-Raycast-Extension/e40b4a7b-5aec-4d3e-946a-bc726edecd6b.jsonl` is 214 bytes containing only `ai-title` + `agent-name`.

native_path=(empty)  origin_cwd=/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension
size=0  mtime=0  index_version=7  indexed_at=2026-07-26T16:08:07Z  deleted=0
```
Caveats to design around: `name`, `native_path` are often empty; `size`/`mtime` are often `0`; `session_id` is the **agent's own session id** (matches Claude's `sessionId` and the JSONL filename — so you can join SpecStory ⇄ `~/.claude/projects/**`). The **same repo can appear under two `project_id`s** (workspace-derived vs git-derived — see `.project.json` below).

FTS works directly:
```sql
select s.agent, s.project_name, s.session_id, s.slug
from sessions_fts f join sessions s on s.session_id=f.session_id and s.agent=f.agent
where sessions_fts match 'raycast' limit 5;
-- claude|dotfiles|ac435a1f-…|project-agent-skills-tmpl
-- claude|dotfiles|fd4d6313-…|antigravity-cli-q-speedtest
```
Note the join can produce duplicate rows (same session matched twice) — dedupe on `(agent, session_id)`.

## 3. Usage / quota

**Nothing usage-specific is installed.** Concretely:
- `ccusage` is **only a shell alias** → `bunx ccusage` (`/Users/david/.local/share/mise/installs/bun/1.3.9/bin/bunx`). No package is cached under `~/.bun`, so it would download on first use — and note `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` plus a localhost proxy is in play.
- `claude-monitor`: not found. `cc-usage`: not found. Nothing usage/quota/cost-named in `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, or `~/.local/share/uv/tools` (that list: ansible-core, apprise, copyparty, git-filter-repo, jupyterlab, litellm, marimo, markitdown, mihome-ctl, mlflow, pre-commit, python-dotenv, specify-cli, sqlit-tui, thefuck, tmuxp, trafilatura, visidata, xonsh, yt-dlp).
- npm global (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.13.1/lib/node_modules`): only `@playwright`, `corepack`, `npm`.

**`claude` CLI has no `usage` subcommand.** Full command list from `claude --help`:
```
agents | auth | auto-mode | doctor | gateway | install | mcp | plugin|plugins
project | setup-token | ultrareview | update|upgrade
```
(`/usage` exists only as an in-TUI slash command, not a CLI subcommand.)

**No `~/.claude/usage` directory or cache exists.** The only quota-adjacent files:
- `/Users/david/.claude/policy-limits.json` — org policy, not consumption: `{"restrictions":{"enforce_web_search_mcp_isolation":{"allowed":false}},"compliance_taints":[],"monitoring_notice":null,"defaults":{"remote_control_at_startup":false}}`
- `/Users/david/.claude/stats-cache.json` — historical daily message/session/tool counts and per-model token totals (see 1.7); **stale since 2026-05-24**.

**How rate-limit data actually reaches a UI here:** Claude Code passes it on **stdin to the statusline command**, and `claude-hud` parses it at `/Users/david/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/0.0.11/src/stdin.ts:138-153`:
```ts
const rateLimits = stdin.rate_limits;
const fiveHour = parseRateLimitPercent(rateLimits.five_hour?.used_percentage);
const sevenDay = parseRateLimitPercent(rateLimits.seven_day?.used_percentage);
… fiveHourResetAt: parseRateLimitResetAt(rateLimits.five_hour?.resets_at),
  sevenDayResetAt: parseRateLimitResetAt(rateLimits.seven_day?.resets_at),
```
with the shape in `src/types.ts:59`:
```ts
export interface UsageData { fiveHour: number|null; sevenDay: number|null;
  fiveHourResetAt: Date|null; sevenDayResetAt: Date|null; }
```
Also `stdin.context_window.current_usage.{input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens}`.

**Implication for a menu-bar app:** quota is *push-only* into a statusline process — there is no file to poll. To surface it outside a session you must either (a) add a statusline/hook shim that writes `rate_limits` to a cache file, or (b) recompute from `message.usage` in the transcripts (ccusage's approach).

### 4.1 herdr v0.7.5 — the highest-value integration target

`herdr — terminal workspace manager for AI coding agents`. Server socket at `/Users/david/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`; `herdr status` reports `server: running, protocol 17`.

Subcommand groups: `api`, `config`, `channel`, `workspace`, `worktree`, `tab`, `notification`, `agent`, `pane`, `session`, `integration`.

`herdr agent` = **Control and inspect agent panes**: `list, get, read, send-keys, prompt, rename, focus, wait, attach, start, explain`.
`herdr api`: `snapshot` (live session snapshot), `schema` (bundled API schema).

**`herdr agent list` returns JSON** — one object per running agent, currently **52 agents**:
```json
{"id":"cli:agent:list","result":{"type":"agent_list","agents":[
 {"agent":"claude",
  "agent_session":{"agent":"claude","kind":"id","source":"herdr:claude",
                   "value":"1b31cf2b-ca09-46d1-a9a9-fb973d135045"},
  "agent_status":"idle",                       // idle | working | blocked | unknown
  "cwd":"/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension",
  "foreground_cwd":"/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension",
  "focused":false,"pane_id":"w3:pN","tab_id":"w3:tF","workspace_id":"w3",

This is the jackpot: **`agent_session.value` is the Claude `sessionId`**, so it joins directly to `~/.claude/projects/**/<sessionId>.jsonl` *and* to `specstory sessions.session_id`. Status values observed live: `idle` (majority), `blocked` (2 agents — SmartHome and openwrt).

```
40:1.1 | 48186 | zsh | /Users/david | Hanrus-MacBook-Pro.local | zsh
vibe/Avalon_Remaster:1.1 | 48248 | zsh | /Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui | :/Users/david/Documents/Program/Avalon_Remaster | agents
vibe/Avalon_Remaster:2.1 | 48303 | zsh | /Users/david/Documents/Program/Avalon_Remaster | Hanrus-MacBook-Pro.local | git
vibe/Avalon_Remaster:3.1 | 48349 | nvim | /Users/david/Documents/Program/Avalon_Remaster | … | edit
vibe/Avalon_Remaster:4.1 | 48394 | zsh | /Users/david/Documents/Program/Avalon_Remaster | ✳ avalon-pwa-implementation | zsh
```
Detection notes:
- `#{pane_current_command}` shows `zsh`, **not** `claude` — Claude Code runs as a child, so command-name matching fails. Use `#{pane_title}`: an agent pane's title is the Claude session title prefixed with **`✳ `** (e.g. `✳ avalon-pwa-implementation`). herdr uses the same marker and helpfully exposes `terminal_title_stripped`.
- Fallback: walk `#{pane_pid}` children (`pgrep -P`) looking for the `claude` binary, or join `#{pane_pid}` against `/Users/david/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` — but note that registry keys on the **claude** PID, not the shell PID, so a `pgrep -P` descent is required.
- `pane_title` is also settable by the shell, so it's advisory (see the pane whose title is a stale `:/Users/david/…` path).

## 6. Cross-source join keys (summary)

- **Claude session uuid** is the universal key: `~/.claude/projects/**/<uuid>.jsonl` filename ⇄ transcript `sessionId` ⇄ `~/.claude/history.jsonl.sessionId` ⇄ `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json.sessionId` ⇄ `~/.claude/tasks/<uuid>/` ⇄ `~/.claude/file-history/<uuid>/` ⇄ `specstory sessions.session_id` (agent='claude') ⇄ `herdr agent list[].agent_session.value`.
- **cwd** joins tmux panes, herdr panes, `specstory sessions.origin_cwd`, `history.jsonl.project`, and the mangled `projects/` dir name (prefer the in-file `cwd`, the dir name is lossy).
- **Title**: transcript `ai-title`/`agent-name`, herdr `terminal_title_stripped`, tmux `pane_title` (all carry the same `✳ <slug>` string), and `sessions.slug` in SpecStory.
- **Missing link**: quota. No local file; only pushed to the statusline via `stdin.rate_limits.{five_hour,seven_day}.{used_percentage,resets_at}`.

 `https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland`

```text
What it is
- CodeIsland is a macOS notch/Dynamic Island utility that shows real‑time status from AI coding agents in a compact panel.  
- Quote (README): "Real-time AI coding agent status panel for macOS Dynamic Island"  

Platform / tech stack
- macOS 14+ (Sonoma) app written in Swift (requires Swift 5.9+ for building).  
- Uses a tiny native Swift bridge binary (codeisland-bridge) and Unix socket IPC for events.  
- Provides optional iPhone / Apple Watch companion apps (source trees under ios/CodeIslandCompanion and apple-companion).

What it displays and how it gets data
- Displays live session information per AI tool: active sessions, tool calls, permission requests, AI replies, mascots, and status icons.  
- Data path: each supported CLI/agent installs a lightweight hook that sends JSON messages over a Unix socket at /tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock to the CodeIsland app. The README’s event flow:  
  - Quote (≤125 chars): "→ Unix socket → /tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock"  
  - Quote (≤125 chars): "codeisland-bridge (native Swift binary, ~86KB)"  
- For OpenCode specifically a JS plugin connects directly to the socket (no bridge binary required).  
- The app listens on the socket, updates the UI in real time, and can publish lightweight snapshots to the iPhone companion over the local network or Bluetooth.

Files / APIs it reads or installs
- Hooks/config placed into each AI tool’s configuration (CLI hooks). The app interacts with:
  - Unix socket at /tmp/codeisland-<uid>.sock for incoming JSON events.
  - Local helper binary (codeisland-bridge) used by CLI hooks.
  - Repository paths shown: Sources/, ios/CodeIslandCompanion, apple-companion, docs/images, and Resources including cli-icons and mascots.
- Build / packaging files present: Package.swift, build.sh, Info.plist, CodeIsland.entitlements, and hook installer logic described in README (auto hook install).

Supported tools (13 listed)
- Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot, Trae/Traecli, Qoder, Factory, CodeBuddy, OpenCode, Kimi Code CLI, Cline, Pi / Oh My Pi.

Key features (extracted and paraphrased)
- Notch-native UI that expands from the MacBook notch and collapses when idle.  
- Live status tracking of agent sessions, tool calls, and replies.  
- Permission management: approve/deny tool permission requests directly from the panel.  
- Inline question answering: reply to agent questions without leaving current app.  
- Pixel-art animated mascots per tool.  
- One-click jump to the associated terminal tab or IDE window.  
- Smart suppress: tab-level terminal detection to avoid over-suppressing notifications.  
- 8‑bit optional sound effects.  
- Automatic hook installation, auto-repair and version tracking for CLI tools.  
- iPhone & Apple Watch buddy: mirrors sessions to Dynamic Island, Lock Screen, StandBy, and Watch.  
- Bilingual UI (English/Chinese), auto-detect language.  
- Multi-display support with notch detection.  
- Configurable keyboard shortcuts (toggle panel, approve/deny, etc.) and a 7-tab settings UI (General, Behavior, Appearance, Mascots, Sound, Hooks, About).

Screenshots / visuals
- Repository includes a notch-panel preview image (docs/images/notch-panel.png) showing a compact pixel-art panel expanded from the MacBook notch.  
- Each AI tool has a small animated mascot (GIFs under docs/images/mascots) and 32×32 cli-icons under Sources/CodeIsland/Resources/cli-icons.

How agent state is detected / monitored
- Each supported CLI/agent triggers a hook event on session start, tool call, permission request, etc. The hook sends a JSON event through the Unix socket to CodeIsland which parses it and updates the UI immediately.  
- The README’s event diagram (paraphrased): agent → hook → codeisland-bridge → Unix socket → CodeIsland app → UI + optional Buddy sync.

- The endpoint is rate‑limited per access token in practice; community reports describe very aggressive per-token throttling (reports of only a few requests before 429s), so clients add caching and conservative polling. I'm finding that the credentials aren't stored in a separate file but rather in the system Keychain under "Claude Code-credentials," and they can be retrieved using the security command-line tool, though accessing them from a new process like Raycast will trigger a macOS permission prompt.

There's also a local proxy running on port 4142 that Claude Code routes through (likely "Agent Maestro" based on the config), but the OAuth usage endpoint would still hit api.anthropic.com directly with the keychain token to report actual subscription quota consumption, regardless of whether the proxy is injecting real credentials or acting as a passthrough.

I'm weighing whether to actually call the usage endpoint now to verify feasibility — it's read-only and harmless on their own account, but it requires reading the keychain secret which triggers a prompt, and it's an outward-facing network call. I think I should flag this as a verification step in the plan rather than doing it immediately, though I could potentially do a cheaper check that doesn't require the secret.

I'm also noting that sqlite3 is reliably at /usr/bin on macOS, not homebrew, so I need to adjust the probe directories accordingly. The SpecStory FTS database is performant and supports snippet extraction, though I'm seeing some data quality issues like empty name fields and missing created_at timestamps for claude rows that I'll need to handle.

Herdr's agent list command is impressively fast at 43ms with 52 agents available, and herdr agent focus works directly without needing workspace context like pane focus does. I'm still investigating whether claude-hud caches rate limits anywhere, and I'm testing whether reading a WAL-mode database in read-only mode works reliably — it seems to work even without creating the shared memory file, which is good for my use case.

I need to check a few more things: whether `immutable=1` is actually safe for this scenario, what's in the user's Raycast extensions directory, how the claude sessions directory compares to herdr's structure, and what the output formats look like for peon status and specstory list when run with JSON output.

I should also check if codex or opencode have their own quota endpoints worth considering.

For the Raycast implementation, shelling out to `/usr/bin/sqlite3` is the pragmatic choice since Raycast doesn't handle native modules well. Reading a WAL database in read-only mode should work fine since the user owns the files and the `-shm` file already exists, though there's a theoretical risk if the WAL is being written concurrently—but in practice that's manageable. === claude-hud stdin.ts rate_limits parsing (exact) ===

  return Math.round(Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value)));

function parseRateLimitResetAt(value: number | null | undefined): Date | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return new Date(value * 1000);
}

export function getUsageFromStdin(stdin: StdinData): UsageData | null {
  const rateLimits = stdin.rate_limits;
  if (!rateLimits) {
    return null;
  }

  const fiveHour = parseRateLimitPercent(rateLimits.five_hour?.used_percentage);
  const sevenDay = parseRateLimitPercent(rateLimits.seven_day?.used_percentage);
  if (fiveHour === null && sevenDay === null) {
    return null;
  }

  return {
    fiveHour,
    sevenDay,
    fiveHourResetAt: parseRateLimitResetAt(rateLimits.five_hour?.resets_at),
    sevenDayResetAt: parseRateLimitResetAt(rateLimits.seven_day?.resets_at),
  };
}

=== codexbar.md ===
# CodexBar CLI

[CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) shows usage stats for AI coding tools (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) without logging into each dashboard.

- **macOS**: Full menu bar app + CLI
- **Linux**: CLI only

## Installation

Installed automatically via the `coding_agents` ansible role. On Linux, the binary is placed at `~/.local/bin/codexbar`.

## Linux Usage

On Linux, you **must** pass `--source cli` for the `usage` command. The default source (`auto`/`web`) is macOS-only.

### Check live usage (rate limits / quotas)

```bash
# Claude session/weekly limits
codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli

# Other providers
codexbar usage --provider codex --source cli
codexbar usage --provider gemini --source cli
codexbar usage --provider copilot --source cli

# JSON output (for scripting / Waybar)
codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli --json --pretty
```

Example output:

```
== Claude 2.1.34 (claude) ==
Session: 14% left [=-----------]
```

### Check local cost (from JSONL logs, no auth needed)

The `cost` command reads local log files (e.g. `~/.claude/`) and doesn't require auth.

```bash
# All providers
codexbar cost

# Claude only
codexbar cost --provider claude

# JSON output
codexbar cost --provider claude --json --pretty

# Force rescan of logs
codexbar cost --refresh
```

Example output:

```
Claude Cost (local)
Today: $0.54 · 851K tokens
Last 30 days: $8.50 · 9.1M tokens
```

## Shell Aliases

Defined in `~/.config/shell/40_codexbar.sh`:

| Alias | Command | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `cbu` | `codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli` | Claude usage |
| `cbc` | `codexbar cost --provider claude` | Claude local cost |
| `cbca` | `codexbar cost` | All providers local cost |

## Supported Providers

`codex`, `claude`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `factory`, `gemini`, `antigravity`, `copilot`, `zai`, `minimax`, `kimi`, `kiro`, `vertexai`, `augment`, `jetbrains`, `kimik2`, `amp`

## Tips

- Avoid `--provider all` with `usage` on Linux -- it tries each provider sequentially and can hang if a CLI isn't installed.
- The `cost` command works offline by scanning local JSONL log files.
- The `usage --source cli` command invokes the provider's CLI (e.g. `claude`) to get live rate-limit data.
- Config file: `~/.codexbar/config.json`
```
</details></tool-use>

=== agent-panes-discovery.md (head) ===
# Agent pane discovery

Find — and jump to — coding-agent sessions (`claude`, `cursor-agent`, `codex`,
`opencode`) that are currently running in *any* tmux pane on this host.

The pain this solves: you start `claude` in pane A on session `chezmoi`, hop
into pane B in another window for a quick test, drift over to a `vibe/foo`
session for a Codex task, and three windows later you can't remember which
pane has the agent you wanted to nudge. CodeIsland (macOS) tells you which
**terminal app** is running an agent, but not the specific tmux pane —
useless once you have more than one agent inside one terminal.

Two complementary surfaces ship in this repo, both backed by tmux:

| Tool | Scope | Best at |
|---|---|---|
| `tv agent-panes` | All four agents (Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor) | "Where am I running stuff?" cross-agent overview, jump-to-pane |
| `tv agent-wakeup` | Same live panes, plus pueue wakeup tasks | "Which agent is quota-blocked, when should I send `continue`?" |
| `recon` (optional) | Claude-only, with live status (Working / Idle / Waiting) parsed from pane capture | "Which Claude needs my attention?" — recon's live status detection is richer than what we replicate in tv |

## `tv agent-panes` (primary)

Open the picker with `prefix + a` inside tmux, or via the popup menu
(`prefix + Space → → Agents → Live agent panes (tv)`), or from any shell
with `tv agent-panes`.

Each row is one running agent pane. The status column shows ● (busy) or
○ (idle) for Claude (read from `~/.claude/sessions/{pid}.json`); blank for
others.

```
[cc] ● chezmoi:1.1     │  discover-coding-agent-sessions          │  chezmoi
[cc] ○ chezmoi:2.1     │  fix-nvm-lazy-loader-permission-request  │  chezmoi
[cc] ●  vibe/foo:4.1   │  refactor auth module                    │  foo
[oc]   vibe/bar:0.0    │  Generate migration script               │  bar
```

### Keybindings (in the picker)

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Alt+T` | Switch tmux focus to that session/window/pane |
| `Alt+K` | Kill the pane (with `[y/N]` confirm) |
| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy the pane target (`session:win.pane`) to clipboard |
| `Alt+P` | Copy directory path |
| `Alt+R` | Copy session ID |
| `Alt+S` | Copy matched `.specstory/history/*.md` path |
| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview: live `tmux capture-pane` snapshot ↔ stored transcript |
| `Esc` | Close the picker |

### How resolution works

- **Claude** — Claude Code writes a per-process file at
  `~/.claude/sessions/{claude_pid}.json` containing `sessionId`, `cwd`,
  `status`, and (when set) a friendly `name`. The discovery walker reads
  these directly — *zero heuristics* for Claude. It then walks each
  `claude_pid`'s parent chain via `ps -o ppid=` until it finds a tmux
  `pane_pid`, which gives the pane target.
- **Codex / OpenCode / Cursor** — `pgrep -x <bin>` finds running agent
  PIDs, parent-chain walked the same way. Session ID is best-effort: the
```

=== agent-overlays.md ===
# Coding-agent CLI overlays (Cursor / OpenCode / Codex)

This repo manages the *global* config files of three coding-agent CLIs via chezmoi `modify_` overlays:

| CLI | Live file | Source script | Merge engine |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` | [`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl`](../../dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
| OpenCode (server/runtime) | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_opencode.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
| OpenCode (TUI) | `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` | [`dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl`](../../dot_config/opencode/modify_tui.json.tmpl) | `jq '. * $overlay'` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | [`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl) | Python `tomllib` + inline emitter |

Overlay payloads live under [`.chezmoitemplates/agents/`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/) and are sourced via `{{ template ... }}` includes so the merge logic can be tested independently of overlay contents.

> **Why not Charm [`crush`](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush)?** `crush` is Charm's own agentic coding CLI. Adding it would mean a fifth overlay (binary + auth + per-project trust + marketplace state), and the cost-of-ownership of each agent overlay is non-trivial — every CLI that rewrites its own config file at runtime needs a hook-aware merger, TOML/JSON round-tripper, and presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. The existing trio (Cursor / OpenCode / Codex, plus Claude Code via `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl`) already covers the practical agent-CLI design space. If you want to evaluate `crush`, the add-a-fifth-CLI pattern is: install in `dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`, add `dot_crush/modify_<config>` plus `.chezmoitemplates/agents/crush.overlay.<json|toml>`, then optionally wire into the `04_ai_capture.zsh` agent-detection chain.

## Why `modify_` and not full file management

All three CLIs **rewrite their config file at runtime** to record machine-local state: auth tokens, telemetry IDs, per-project trust grants, marketplace registrations with absolute paths, plugin-cache hashes, last-used provider hints, etc. Tracking the whole file as managed content would:

1. Leak secrets (`authInfo`, `auth.json` content) into the dotfiles repo.
2. Bake one machine's absolute paths (`/Users/me/.codex/.tmp/...`) into another machine's apply.
3. Produce constant `chezmoi diff` noise as the CLI churns the file.

The `modify_` overlay model deep-merges only the keys we explicitly enforce; everything else passes through verbatim.

## What each overlay enforces

### Cursor — [`agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/cursor.cli-config.overlay.json)

```json
{
  "editor": { "vimMode": true }
}
```

- `editor.vimMode = true` — universal preference; sibling `editor.fontSize` etc. survive the deep merge.
- **`permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` arrays are intentionally NOT in the overlay.** `jq '. * $overlay'` replaces arrays wholesale at the same key path, so listing any entries here would clobber the user's live machine-specific allow-list on every `chezmoi apply`. Manage those per machine via the live file directly, or move to a `--argjson allow $merged` array-union approach if you ever need a shared baseline.

### OpenCode — [`agents/opencode.overlay.json`](../../.chezmoitemplates/agents/opencode.overlay.json)

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "autoupdate": true,
  "default_agent": "build",
  "small_model": "github-copilot/gpt-5-mini",
  "agent": { "title": { "reasoningEffort": "low" } },
  "provider": {
    "github-copilot": {
      "options": { "timeout": 600000 }

# Agent Deck — a Raycast quick menu for AI coding agents

## 0. What I actually measured (corrections to the brief)

Everything below is from this machine, today. Four of these contradict the brief and change the design.

| Claim | Measured | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `herdr agent list` 0.043 s / 52 agents | **0.052 s**, 52 agents, 50 idle / 2 blocked, all `claude` | confirmed; menu-bar-cheap |
| SpecStory FTS "cold = 0.11 s" | rank-only query **22–65 ms warm**, **3.5 s cold** (290 MB db + 36 MB WAL) | fine, but the first query after login pays 3.5 s — needs a warm-up |
| `snippet(sessions_fts, 3, …)` "works" | works, but costs **0.20–3.4 s per query**, dominated by matched body size (avg **263 KB**, max **10.4 MB**) | **snippet can never be on the typeahead path.** This is the single biggest design constraint |
| dedupe `(agent, session_id)` | **81 groups have >1 FTS row, max 6** | naive join fans out 6× |
| `bm25(sessions_fts)` in a CTE/aggregate | **fails**: `Error: stepping, unable to use function bm25 in the requested context` | must use the magic `rank` column instead |
| empty `updated_at` | **7 rows**, and they are *exactly* the `project_id='unknown'` rows — also empty `created_at`, `origin_cwd`, `slug` | those rows have FTS bodies but zero metadata |
| same repo, two `project_id`s | confirmed, and it is **this repo** (`b1f0-…` workspace, `f1dd-…` git) | never group by `project_id`; group by `origin_cwd` |
| `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` all alive | **49 files, 49 alive, 48 distinct sessionIds** — pids 21952 and 95663 **share one sessionId** (one idle, one busy) | `sessionId` is a 1:N link to live processes, **not** a primary key |
| statuses | herdr `AgentStatus` enum from `herdr api schema --json` = `["idle","working","blocked","done","unknown"]`; claude registry uses `idle`/`busy` and `kind: interactive`/`bg` | two vocabularies, needs normalization |
| `herdr agent focus <target>` | target accepts **`pane_id` only** (`w3:p7`). `terminal_id`, the session UUID, and the title all return `agent_not_found` | pane_id is the actuator handle |
| herdr errors | **structured JSON**: `{"error":{"code":"agent_not_found","message":"…"},"id":"cli:agent:get"}`, exit 1 | far better than pueue's prose stderr — `code` maps straight to an error `kind` |
| herdr with no socket | printed `Error: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, … }` — **not** JSON | must classify on "stdout doesn't parse", not on exit code |
| local usage scan | 24 h = 121 files / **222 MB** / **4.4 s**; 7 d = 804 files / 355 MB / **26 s** (grep alone) | needs an incremental index; not a v0.1 feature |
| the proxy | `bun` listening on 4142, HTTP 200; `settings.local.json` sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=dummy`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`. **Claude Code's own transcripts contain `"model":"gemini-2.5-pro"`** (3 records / 7 d) alongside `claude-opus-4-8` (30 359) and `claude-opus-5` (13 290) | an Anthropic quota meter would be **actively wrong** on this machine |
| the join | **52/52** live herdr session UUIDs exist in the SpecStory DB **and** have a `~/.claude/projects/*/<uuid>.jsonl`; 46/52 in the registry | the join is real and total. This is the product |
| binaries | `herdr` `~/.local/bin`, `specstory`/`peon`/`codex`/`gemini`/`pueue` `/usr/local/bin`, `claude`/`cursor-agent` `~/.local/bin`, **`opencode` at `~/.opencode/bin`**, `sqlite3` **only** at `/usr/bin` (no Homebrew build) | `~/.opencode/bin` is **not** in the reference PROBE_DIRS |
| Raycast runtime | Node 22 (per the vendored skill) | `node:sqlite` landed in 22.5 **behind `--experimental-sqlite`**, and Raycast cannot pass flags → **shell out to `/usr/bin/sqlite3`** (3.51.0, `ENABLE_FTS5`, `-json` works) |

---

## 1. Feasibility verdict per capability

### 1. Search chat history — **SHIP IT. This is the product.**

Strong, and stronger than any prior art. The SpecStory DB is a single pre-built global FTS5 index across claude/codex/gemini (470 sessions), the rank query is 22–65 ms, and the results join cleanly to live panes. The extension is a thin, honest client.

**Risks, in order:**
- **`snippet()` cost.** 0.2–3.4 s per call, superlinear in body size. Mitigation: snippet is off the typeahead path entirely, and off by default (preference, with the measurement in its description).
- **Cold-start 3.5 s.** The first query after a reboot pays for faulting in the b-tree. Mitigation: fire a throwaway `SELECT count(*) FROM sessions` at view mount, before the user has typed.
- **FTS5 syntax.** A user typing `-x` gets `no such column: x`; `foo"` gets `unterminated string`; `col:x` gets `no such column: col`. **A raw user string is not an FTS5 expression** — must be tokenized and quoted.
- **The DB is a third party's private schema.** SpecStory can change it. Mitigation: pin `index_version`, and degrade to the claude-fs path when the schema doesn't match.
- **288 MB, hot WAL.** Read-only `file:…?mode=ro` worked against the live WAL with no contention. Keep `mode=ro`; never open read-write.

### 2. Live agent state — **SHIP IT, with a fallback that makes it store-viable.**

herdr is fast, structured, and its errors carry codes. But herdr is not something a store user has. The design decision that matters: **herdr is an enhancement, not a requirement.** `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` + `ps -p` gives a complete Claude-only live view with zero dependencies, and it covered 46 of the 52 herdr agents plus 3 herdr can't see.

**Risks:**
- **herdr's status is screen-scraped.** `herdr agent explain w3:p7` returns `rule: live_prompt_box (region=prompt_box_body priority=950), evidence: "❯\n"`. It is inferring state from rendered terminal text. It will occasionally be wrong, and it will lag a real state change by however long its detection poll is. **Do not present it as ground truth** — present it with a "detected" framing and offer `herdr agent explain` as an action.
- **`cwd` is the pane's shell cwd, not the project.** 8 of 52 agents report `/Users/david`. Use `origin_cwd` from the joined SpecStory row when it disagrees.
- **`terminal_title` is absent on 6 of 52.** Title fallback chain required.
- **The reconcile delay is unmeasured.** The 400 ms / 1500 ms constants in the reference repo are pueued's. herdr's screen-scrape loop is a different animal. **This must be measured before `optimistic.ts` is trusted** (method in §10).
- **Jump-to-terminal is two steps.** `herdr agent focus w3:p7` moves herdr's focus inside its own session; the host app (**Alacritty** here, pid 516) still has to be raised with `/usr/bin/open -a`.

### 3. Quota — **WEAK. Do not ship in v0.1. Ship a differently-named thing in v0.3.**

This is the honest verdict and I'll defend it below in §6. Summary: there is no local rate-limit file (`policy-limits.json` is org policy; `stats-cache.json` last computed 25 May); the OAuth endpoint needs a keychain ACL prompt from a launchd process plus aggressive 429s; codexbar isn't installed; and **the proxy makes the Anthropic number the wrong number anyway** — I found Gemini traffic inside Claude Code's own transcripts.

### 4. Small tools — **peon YES (v0.2, trivial), pueue YES (v0.2, already have the code), specstory YES (already the search backbone).**

`peon status` is 6 lines of plain text with a stable shape; the whole integration is a 40-line parser plus 4 menu items. `pueue` `agent-wakeup` is a genuinely good fit for "this agent is quota-blocked, poke it in 3 h" — but note the `agent-wakeup` group **does not currently exist** (`pueue group` shows only `default`), so the action must create it.

---

## 2. Repo name

| Repo | package.json `name` / `title` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **`Agent-Deck-Raycast-Extension`** ← recommended | `agent-deck` / **Agent Deck** | "deck" = flight deck / control deck. Reads as observability, not as another agent. Short, free on the store, no collision with herdr/CodexBar/ClaudeCast |
| `Roost-Raycast-Extension` | `roost` / **Roost** | where the flock rests; pairs with herdr's metaphor. Cuter, less searchable |
| `Agent-Switchboard-Raycast-Extension` | `agent-switchboard` / **Agent Switchboard** | most literal about the routing job. Long; "switchboard" is dated |

Matches the sibling's convention (`Pueue-Raycast-Extension`, `github.com/daviddwlee84/…`), `author: "da-wei_lee"`, `license: MIT`, `categories: ["Developer Tools", "Productivity"]`, `platforms: ["macOS"]`.

**Description** (store-facing, differentiating): *"Find any past AI coding session by what was said in it, see which agents are running or waiting on you right now, and jump straight back into either — across Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI."*

**Differentiation from prior art**, to write into `docs/prior-art.md`: ccusage is cost-only; Threadlens/claude-history/raycast-claude-sessions are search-only; ClaudeCast is remote-control-only. **None of them has a menu bar, and none of them joins a search result to a live process you can focus.** That join — verified 52/52 here — is the whole thesis.

---

## 3. Commands (package.json)

### v0.1

```
agent-menu     menu-bar  interval "1m"   "Agents Menu Bar"
sessions       view      arg: query      "Search Agent Sessions"
agents         view                      "Live Agents"
focus-agent    no-view   arg: target*    "Focus Agent"
```

**`agent-menu`** — the headline. Icon tinted red when `blocked > 0`.
- Sections: **Blocked** (needs you) → **Working** → **Idle** (collapsed into per-project submenus, hidden behind a preference) → "Updated HH:MM" label row → "Search Sessions…" / "Live Agents" launchers.
- 50 idle agents is the real scaling problem. `maxItemsPerSection` default 7; idle grouped by `basename(origin_cwd ?? cwd)`.
- Per-agent items: **Focus** (default), **Read Last 40 Lines** (pushes nothing — copies to clipboard, since the menu can't render a Detail), **Copy Resume Command**, ⌥ **Explain Detection**.
- Preferences: `titleCounts` dropdown (`blocked` | `blocked-working` | `working` | `none`, default `blocked`), `maxItemsPerSection` (7), `showIdle` checkbox (default **off** — 50 items), `groupIdleByProject` checkbox (on).
- `updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle: "2 blocked · 0 working · 50 idle" })` in `onData`.

**`sessions`** — the search view. `List` with `throttle`, `isShowingDetail` toggled by ⌘⇧D.
- Argument `query` (text, optional) seeds `searchText`.
- Accessories: agent tag, project name, relative time, and a **`LIVE`** tag when the session has ≥1 running process.
- Actions: **Resume in New Tab** (⏎), **Focus Running Agent** (⌘⏎, only when live), **Copy Resume Command**, **Open Transcript in Editor**, **Copy Session ID**, **Show in Finder**, **Reveal Markdown** (when `.specstory/history/*.md` exists).
- Preferences: `maxResults` (30), `showSnippets` checkbox **default off** — description carries the measurement: *"Highlights the matching text. Costs one extra query per selection, measured at 0.2–3.4 s depending on how large that session is (the largest here is 10 MB). Off by default because the list stays instant without it."*; `historySources` dropdown (`specstory` | `specstory+prompts` | `prompts-only`).

**`agents`** — the live list, with detail. Detail pane shows `herdr agent read --lines 40` output in a fence, plus cwd / git branch / model / joined session title / last prompt.
- Actions: **Focus** (⏎), **Send Prompt** (form), **Wait for Idle** (`herdr agent wait`), **Schedule Wakeup** (pueue, v0.2), **Explain Detection**, **Open Session in Search**.
- `searchBarAccessory`: a status dropdown (All / Blocked / Working / Idle).

**`focus-agent`** — root-search jump. Argument `target` (required): matched against `terminal_title_stripped`, then `basename(cwd)`, then `pane_id`, then the joined session title. Single match → focus + `showHUD`. Multiple → `launchCommand("agents", { context: { filter } })`.

### v0.2

```
agent-sounds   no-view                   "Toggle Agent Sounds"   (peon)
```

### v0.3

```
usage          view                      "Agent Usage"
```

### Extension-level preferences

| name | type | note |
|---|---|---|
| `liveSource` | dropdown | `auto` (default) / `herdr` / `claude-registry` / `both`. `auto` = herdr if the server answers, else the registry |
| `herdrPath` | textfield | placeholder `/Users/you/.local/bin/herdr`. Description names the launchd PATH trap |
| `sqlitePath` | textfield | placeholder `/usr/bin/sqlite3`. Description: *"macOS ships 3.51 with FTS5 and `-json`, which is all this needs. Homebrew does not install one by default."* |
| `specstoryDb` | textfield | default `~/.specstory/sessions.db` |
| `claudeHome` | textfield | honours `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, default `~/.claude` |
| `agentFilter` | textfield | `claude, codex, gemini` — empty = all. `;`-separated (Raycast preferences **cannot be multiline**, see the sibling repo's pitfall) |
| `terminalApp` | appPicker | raised with `/usr/bin/open -a` after `herdr agent focus`. Detected once from the herdr server's ancestor process; Alacritty here |
| `confirmDestructive` | checkbox | same semantics as the sibling: dialog in views, ⌥-hold in the menu bar |
